en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Those Who Have Never Been Maidens, 78.
The Second Training Rule on Not Ordaining a Sikkhamānā.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain *sikkhamānā* approached the bhikkhunī Thullanandā and requested full ordination (*upasampadā*).

The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said to that *sikkhamānā*, "If you, noble lady, will follow me for two years, then I shall ordain you. Having said this, she neither ordained her nor made any effort to have her ordained.
Then that *sikkhamānā* reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires… were indignant, disparaged, and complained, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā say to a trainee nun, ‘If you, noble lady,
will follow me for two years, then I will give you the full admission,’ and yet neither give her the full admission nor make any effort to have her admitted?”… [as before]…
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā said to a trainee nun,
‘If you, noble lady, will follow me for two years, I will ordain you,’ and yet neither ordained her nor made any effort to have her ordained?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:

“… How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having said to a trainee nun, ‘If you, noble lady, will follow me for two years, then I will give you the full admission,’ neither give her the full admission nor make any effort to have her admitted? …”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
‘Whatever nun should say to a trainee nun: “If you, noble lady, will follow me for two years...”’”
‘I shall indeed cause her to be ordained,’ yet afterwards, being without obstacle, she neither ordains her nor makes an effort to have her ordained—
this is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). “But who,” means:
Whichever [nun], of whatever kind …pe… “a nun” …pe… this is the nun intended in this context.
A *sikkhamānā* is one who has trained for two years in the six rules. "If you,
noble lady, will follow me for two years..."
"You shall attend upon me for two years;
in this way I will have you disrobed,
and in this way I will have you ordained."
"She afterwards, being without obstacle" means in the absence of an obstacle.
"She should not ordain" means... [as above].
"One should not ordain oneself;
one should not make an effort to have another ordained" means that one should not command another to do so.
“I will neither cause her to be ordained nor make an effort toward her ordination”— at the mere moment of relinquishing this burden, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense if there is an obstacle.
If one does not obtain [the requisites] after searching for them,
or in the case of illness,
or in times of misfortune.
[The offense applies to] one who is insane, and to one who is a first-offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
